usdRate.sourceName: Swiss National Bank, foreign exchange rates, monthly average (cube devkum)
usdRate.note: CHF 0.82854 per USD, October 2026 monthly average (September 0.81926); World Bank 2025 average 0.83.

inflation_cpi.sourceName: Trading Economics, Switzerland inflation rate (FSO CPI, secondary source)
inflation_cpi.note: CPI up 1.0% year on year in September 2026 (0.8% in August); the Federal Statistical Office pages were being moved and could not be read. Eurostat HICP for Switzerland: 1.2%.

inflation_projection.sourceName: SNB price stability defined as CPI inflation of 0-2%; CPI 1.0% in September 2026, World Bank 2025 average 0.15%
inflation_projection.note: Swiss inflation has averaged about 1% over the past five years including the 2022 spike, the middle of the SNB's 0-2% range, so 1% is used.

policy_rate.sourceName: Swiss National Bank, official interest rates (data portal cube snboffzisa)
policy_rate.note: SNB policy rate 0% (unchanged since June 2025); Trading Economics also shows 0% at end-October 2026.

savings_account_rate.sourceName: Swiss National Bank, interest rates on new business by product (cube zikrepro): private clients' savings deposits, mean
savings_account_rate.note: Average 0.069% in September 2026 (0.069% in August); payment accounts without withdrawal restrictions pay about 0%.

fdr_3m_rate.sourceName: Swiss National Bank, interest rates on new business (zikrepro): term deposits of CHF 100,000 or more, 3 months, mean
fdr_3m_rate.note: Average 0.029% in September 2026; 1-month term deposits averaged -0.03%. Series covers deposits of at least CHF 100,000.

fdr_1y_rate.sourceName: Swiss National Bank, interest rates on new business (zikrepro): term deposits of CHF 100,000 or more, 12 months, mean
fdr_1y_rate.note: Average 0.152% in September 2026 (0.117% in August); bank cash bonds (Kassenobligationen) paid 0.49% for 2 years and 0.70% for 5 years. Series covers deposits of at least CHF 100,000.

dps_rate.note: Swiss banks do not sell a standard monthly recurring deposit product with a published rate; regular saving goes into savings accounts or tax-favoured tied pension (pillar 3a) accounts.

bank_deposit_avg_rate.sourceName: World Bank WDI FR.INR.DPST (deposit interest rate)
bank_deposit_avg_rate.note: 0.083% average for 2025; SNB new-business savings deposits averaged 0.07% in August 2026.

sanchayapatra_5y_rate.note: The Confederation does not sell a retail savings certificate or savings bond to individuals; Confederation bonds and money-market debt register claims are auctioned to market participants. Bank cash bonds (Kassenobligationen) are bank products.

tbill_91d_rate.sourceName: Swiss National Bank, money market rates (cube zimoma): 3-month Confederation money-market debt register claims
tbill_91d_rate.note: Yield -0.047% in September 2026 (monthly average); SARON was -0.07%.

tbond_5y_rate.note: The SNB stopped publishing Confederation bond yields by maturity on its data portal after July 2025, and Trading Economics shows only the 2-year (0.18%) and 10-year yields; no current 5-year yield could be read.

tbond_10y_rate.sourceName: Trading Economics, Switzerland 10-year government bond yield
tbond_10y_rate.note: Secondary source; the SNB's own yield series ended in July 2025. 2-year yield 0.18%.

tax_bank_interest.sourceName: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries, Switzerland income determination
tax_bank_interest.note: Interest on Swiss bank accounts bears 35% withholding tax, credited or refunded when the interest is declared; it is then taxed with other income at ordinary federal, cantonal and communal rates.

tax_sanchayapatra_profit.note: No retail government savings certificate exists; interest on Confederation bonds bears the same 35% withholding tax and ordinary income tax.

deposit_insurance_limit.sourceName: esisuisse (Swiss deposit protection scheme), the Swiss system
deposit_insurance_limit.note: CHF 100,000 per client per bank; tied pension (pillar 3a) and vested-benefits deposits get a separate CHF 100,000.

credit_card_rate_cap.note: The Consumer Credit Ordinance sets maximum interest rates for consumer credit, overdrafts and credit cards, but the Fedlex text could not be read (script-only page), so the current cap is not confirmed.

equity_return_low.sourceName: SMI 14,811 on 30 Oct 2026, +21% over the year and at an all-time high (Trading Economics)
equity_return_low.note: Low case: from record highs, Swiss shares return only about 2% a year.

equity_return_base.sourceName: SMI (Trading Economics); 1-year term deposit 0.15% after tax about 0.1% (SNB zikrepro)
equity_return_base.note: Base capped at the after-tax safe rate plus 4 points; with near-zero Swiss interest rates and a moderate decade for the SMI, 4% in francs is used.

equity_return_high.sourceName: SMI long-run record; long-run global equity returns in francs
equity_return_high.note: High case: diversified Swiss and global equity funds matching their long-run record in francs, held back by the strong franc.

gold_return_low.sourceName: Gold price history (Trading Economics); franc appreciation against the dollar
gold_return_low.note: Low case: gold flat in francs as the franc keeps rising against the dollar after the 2025-26 spike.

gold_return_base.sourceName: Gold price history (Trading Economics); SNB 0-2% price stability
gold_return_base.note: Base case: dollar gold rises with world inflation, partly offset by a slowly appreciating franc.

gold_return_high.note: High case: a repeat of gold's strong 2005-2025 trend in franc terms.

fixed_income_return_low.sourceName: Savings deposits 0.07% (SNB zikrepro) less income tax
fixed_income_return_low.note: Low case: easy-access savings pay essentially nothing after tax.

fixed_income_return_base.sourceName: 12-month term deposits 0.15% less income tax (SNB zikrepro, September 2026)
fixed_income_return_base.note: Base case: the after-tax 1-year deposit rate, about 0.1%.

fixed_income_return_high.sourceName: 10-year Confederation bond 0.47% and 5-year cash bonds 0.70%, less income tax
fixed_income_return_high.note: High case: locking in longer Confederation bonds or bank cash bonds, after tax.

life_claim_settlement_rate.note: FINMA does not publish an industry-wide life insurance claim settlement ratio that could be found.

insurance_term_premium_table.note: Term life cover (Todesfallrisikoversicherung) is sold, but no regulator or official premium table per CHF 1,000 of cover was found.

health_hospitalisation_cost.sourceName: Federal Office of Public Health, premiums and costs FAQ (cost sharing in compulsory health insurance)
health_hospitalisation_cost.note: Computed for an adult with the standard deductible: CHF 300 deductible plus the 10% co-payment cap of CHF 700 plus CHF 15 a day hospital contribution for 5 nights; with the highest deductible (CHF 2,500) it would be CHF 3,275.

health_premium_table.note: Compulsory basic health insurance premiums are flat per person by canton, age group and deductible (average CHF 412 a month in 2027, FOPH), not priced per CHF 100,000 of cover; no such premium table exists.

goal_inflation_health.sourceName: FOPH: basic health insurance premiums up 5.0% on average for 2027; Eurostat HICP health +0.2% in September 2026
goal_inflation_health.note: Health prices in the CPI barely move, but premiums and cost sharing, which households actually pay, have risen 4-6% a year, so 4% is used.

goal_inflation_education.sourceName: Eurostat HICP Switzerland, education (CP10): -0.1% year on year in September 2026
goal_inflation_education.note: Public schooling is free and university fees are low; private school and course fees are planned at about 1.5%, slightly above general inflation.

life_expectancy.sourceName: Eurostat, life expectancy by age and sex (demo_mlexpec), Switzerland
life_expectancy.note: Men 82.4, women 85.9 in 2024; World Bank 2024 total 84.41.

life_table_remaining.sourceName: Eurostat, life expectancy by age and sex (demo_mlexpec), Switzerland 2024

support_ratio.sourceName: Eurostat EUROPOP2023 projections, old-age dependency ratio (proj_23ndbi, baseline), Switzerland
support_ratio.note: 100 divided by the projected old-age dependency ratio (65+ per 100 aged 15-64): 31.2 in 2026, 41.1 in 2040, 52.0 in 2065. World Bank 2025: 31.6.

retirement_age_default.sourceName: Information Centre OASI/DI, leaflet 3.01 Old-age pensions (2026)
retirement_age_default.note: Reference age 65 for men; for women it rises from 64 to 65 between 2025 and 2028 (born 1964 or later: 65), so 65 for anyone born after 1975. Pension can be drawn from 63 or deferred up to 5 years.

retirement_age_government.note: Federal and cantonal staff generally retire at the OASI reference age under their own personnel and pension-fund rules; no single official retirement age for government service could be confirmed from a readable source.

retirement_return_low.note: Low case: easy-access savings pay nothing after tax.

retirement_return_base.sourceName: 12-month term deposits 0.15% less tax (SNB zikrepro, September 2026)
retirement_return_base.note: Base case capped at the after-tax 1-year term deposit rate (about 0.1% after a 25-35% marginal income tax).

retirement_return_high.note: High case: a ladder of longer Confederation bonds and cash bonds after tax.

retirement_accumulation_return_low.sourceName: After-tax deposit rate about 0.1%; equity low 2%
retirement_accumulation_return_low.note: Low case for a balanced mix if shares lag.

retirement_accumulation_return_base.sourceName: After-tax deposit rate about 0.1%; equity base 4%
retirement_accumulation_return_base.note: Base case: roughly half shares at 4% and half safe fixed income near zero after tax.

retirement_accumulation_return_high.note: High case for a growth-leaning balanced mix.

old_age_allowance_monthly.note: There is no flat non-contributory old-age pension: every resident contributes to OASI (AHV), whose full pension is CHF 1,260-2,520 a month in 2026. Low-income pensioners can claim means-tested supplementary benefits (Ergänzungsleistungen), which top income up to a needs level and have no fixed monthly amount.

old_age_allowance_eligibility.note: Supplementary benefits (Ergänzungsleistungen) are paid to OASI pensioners whose income does not cover basic needs (means-tested, with residence conditions for foreign nationals), but the ahv-iv.ch page and leaflet with the rules could not be read.

gratuity_rule.note: No days-per-year gratuity: the Code of Obligations (art. 339b) gives a one-off severance only to employees aged 50+ with 20+ years' service, largely replaced by occupational pension (BVG) savings, which does not fit a days-per-year rule.

public_pension_scheme.sourceName: Information Centre OASI/DI, leaflet 3.01 Old-age pensions (2026)
public_pension_scheme.note: OASI (AHV/AVS), compulsory for all residents: a full pension needs contributions every year from age 20 to the reference age (scale 44). Full pension CHF 1,260-2,520 a month in 2026 plus a 13th monthly payment from December 2026. Adjusted every two years by the mixed index of wages and prices; taxed as income. Occupational pension (BVG) is the compulsory second pillar.

dps.note: No standard recurring-deposit product; regular saving goes into savings or tied pillar 3a accounts.

sanchayapatra_5y.note: No retail government savings certificate; bank cash bonds (Kassenobligationen) are bank products.

tbill_91d.note: Auctioned in large lots, mainly to institutions.

tbond_5y.note: Listed on the Swiss exchange and buyable through a bank.

equity_fund.note: Widely available; capital gains for private investors are generally tax-free, dividends taxed as income.

gold.note: Freely bought; investment gold is exempt from VAT.

insuranceComplaints.name: Ombudsman of Private Insurance (Swiss insurance ombudsman foundation)
insuranceComplaints.note: Health-insurance complaints go to the separate ombudsman for social health insurance.

pensionScheme.name: Old-age and survivors' insurance (OASI / AHV / AVS)

oldAgeAllowance.name: Supplementary benefits to OASI (Ergänzungsleistungen / prestations complémentaires)
oldAgeAllowance.note: Means-tested top-up, not a flat social pension.

publicHealthCover.name: Compulsory health insurance (KVG/LAMal), Federal Office of Public Health
publicHealthCover.note: Basic insurance is compulsory for all residents and bought from approved insurers; premium subsidies for low incomes.
